case_title: Sheesh Ram And Ors. v. The State Of Rajasthan
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 rlw s.34; IPC s.307 rlw s.149
aggravating_circumstances: Previous enmity between the complainant and accused
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under Sections 148, 302 r/w Section 149 and Section 307 r/w section 149 IPC
high_court_outcome: Acquitted four accused of all the offences; convicted others under different sections
offence_finally_established: Murder under Section 302 r/w Section 34 IPC and Section 307 r/w Section 34 IPC
neutral_facts: The prosecution case was that the accused and the complainant were on inimical terms due to land disputes and an earlier murder case. On the fateful day, the complainant was standing with his sons on the roadside. The offenders were on a tractor and stopped to attack them. The complainant and one of his sons ran towards the village. The accused gravely assaulted the elder son of the complainant and killed him. They then ran after the other son of the complainant and inflicted injuries on him, considering him dead, and left the place. The trial court found all the accused guilty and convicted them under Sections 148, 302 r/w Section 149 and Section 307 r/w Section 149 IPC. The High Court acquitted four accused of all the offences and convicted others under different sections. The Supreme Court upheld the conviction of the accused, finding the evidence of the injured witness reliable and consistent, and that the exaggeration in the evidence did not change the prosecution story.
